messages:
alex: Heads-up — I'm seeing a regression in kernel routing telemetry after yesterday's autotune landing. p95 latency up ~15% on seq_len 256-512 buckets. dumping a short trace + logs here.

mira: ugh. which flag set did you run with? AUTOTUNE_ALPHA changes landed, right?

alex: yeah AUTOTUNE_ALPHA=1.2 in canary. logs show the runtime choosing matmul_v2 for ampere at seq_bucket=512 but the reason field says "latency_estimate" even though profiler suggests throughput path would've been cheaper.

samir: can you paste the telemetry line? want to see the full key/value set.

alex: sure — here's one line from the trace export (sanitized):

```
[telemetry] ts=2165512345 request_id=req-9f3a kernel_choice={name:matmul_v2, reason:latency_estimate, est_p50_ms:6.4, est_p95_ms:18.2, cost_score:12.1} arch=ampere seq_bucket=512 kv_cache_hit=false batching_hint=single flags=[AUTOTUNE_ALPHA=1.2,SEQLEN_TUNER=enabled]
```

julia: key bits: seq_bucket=512 and kv_cache_hit=false. if KV cache had hits we may prefer a different kernel. seems autotune isn't weighting kv_cache impact properly.

mira: I think the autotuner's cost model assumes a steady-state KV hit ratio. for short bursts it's wrong. we should expose a debug flag to log the tuner inputs and the fallback scoring so we can repro. e.g. RUNTIME_KERNEL_TUNER_DEBUG=1.

alex: added a small patch locally to dump the tuner inputs. here's env snippet to repro locally: 

```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_route,kv_cache
export RUNTIME_KERNEL_TUNER_DEBUG=1
export AUTOTUNE_ALPHA=1.2
./run-inference --model redwood-7b --seq-len 512 --batch 1
```

perf-bot: [perf alert] Canary deploy 2026-03-17T22:10 UTC: autotune-alpha=1.2 triggered increased p95 for model redwood-7b on region us-west-2. CI trace: https://perf/trace/2165512345

samir: can we get a small reproducer? maybe a short script that toggles kv cache hit/miss and compares chosen kernels. i can write a harness tomorrow.

mira: also want to check batch heuristics — the router seemed to prefer latency path even when batch>1 due to incorrect batching_hint propagation in the request wrapper. maybe a bug in request meta merging.

alex: found one log line where request.meta.batch=4 but routing_ctx.batch_hint=1. suspicious. dump: 

```
[router] request_id=req-9f3a meta.batch=4 merged.batch_hint=1
```

julia: that would definitely bias towards low-batch kernels. please add an assert in the merge codepath and a unit test.

samir: I'll open a quick PR to disable the new alpha in canary while we debug. PR: https://git/repo/pulls/4721 — will revert the rollout knob for alpha.

alex: thanks. i'll attach the fuller trace and a zipped profiler output to the PR. profiler shows kernel matmul_v2 doing lots of small memcopies at seq=512 — cost model underestimated memory overhead.

mira: proposal: extend telemetry to include tuner_inputs and final_score vector. new field names: tuner_inputs={seq_bucket,arch,kv_hit_rate,batch_est} final_scores=[latency_score,throughput_score,cache_penalty]. that will make offline analysis easier.

julia: agree. also add a debug env flag RUNTIME_KERNEL_TRACE=score,reason to make the router emit human-readable decision lines. keep it off by default.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0317-02 by alex — autotune canary latency regressions. severity: low. assignees: eng-runtime.

samir: ok i've paused the canary and queued a rollback. will post rollout status in 10m.

alex: thx. i'll prioritize a small telemetry change and the unit test. attaching the sanitized trace in the PR comments.

mira: if anyone's debugging locally, here's a quick grep that helped me find the merge bug: `rg "merged.batch_hint" -n src/router | sed -n '1,50p'`

julia: once we have the telemetry fields we should add an eval that simulates mixed kv hit ratios to ensure the tuner picks stable choices.

alex: agreed. i'll sketch an eval harness after lunch.

samir: rollback done. canary traffic back to baseline. monitoring -> p95 trending down. will keep it paused until we ship the fix. :thumbsup:

alex: great — thanks all. will keep updates here.
